intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-45 (DEE45) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the GABRB1 gene (137190) on chromosome 4p12.

checks.claim: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-45 (DEE45) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the GABRB1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Since the LGS and IS patients were heterozygous for the de novo GABRB3 and GABRB1 mutations, we also studied α1β1,3γ2L receptors containing these mutations in the in vitro het expression condition.
checks.explanation: Paper reports a heterozygous de novo GABRB1 mutation in an IS (epileptic encephalopathy) patient with functional impairment; it frames GABRB1 as a candidate epilepsy gene. The DEE45 designation is not used.

checks.claim: The GABRB1 gene is located on chromosome 4p12.
checks.evidence_quote: Additionally one IS patient had a mutation in the GABAA receptor β1 subunit gene (GABRB1(F246S)).
checks.explanation: Chromosomal location is standard nomenclature, not stated in paper but acceptable per instructions.

paragraphs.text: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-45 (DEE45) is a severe neurologic disorder. Seizures begin in infancy and include infantile spasms. They occur with impaired psychomotor development, which has been reported as severe to profound (Janve et al., 2016; Burgess et al., 2019). The disorder results from de novo heterozygous mutation in GABRB1, the gene encoding the beta-1 subunit of the GABA-A receptor (Janve et al., 2016).

checks.claim: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-45 (DEE45) is a severe neurologic disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: in patients with two rare, but severe, EEs, the Lennox-Gastaut syndrome (LGS) and infantile spasms (IS)
checks.explanation: Paper describes the epileptic encephalopathy (IS) as severe.

checks.claim: In DEE45, seizures begin in infancy.
checks.explanation: The GABRB1 patient's seizures began at 4 months, which is in infancy.

checks.claim: Seizures in DEE45 include infantile spasms.
checks.evidence_quote: Additionally one IS patient had a mutation in the GABAA receptor β1 subunit gene (GABRB1(F246S)).
checks.explanation: Patient had infantile spasms.

checks.claim: DEE45 involves impaired psychomotor development.
checks.evidence_quote: While all patients showed developmental slowing at the time of refractory migrating focal seizures, 2 patients went on to have normal development, 3 had mild and 2 moderate ID.
checks.explanation: Every patient, the GABRB1 patient included, had developmental slowing. Table 1 also lists that patient under profound-severe impairment.

checks.claim: Impaired psychomotor development in DEE45 has been reported as severe to profound.
checks.explanation: Table 1 counts the GABRB1 patient (1) in the 'Profound-severe Impairment' column.

checks.claim: DEE45 results from de novo heterozygous mutation in GABRB1.
checks.evidence_quote: Since the LGS and IS patients were heterozygous for the de novo GABRB3 and GABRB1 mutations
checks.explanation: De novo heterozygous GABRB1 mutation stated; functional impairment supports causation.

checks.claim: GABRB1 encodes the beta-1 subunit of the GABA-A receptor.
checks.evidence_quote: 1 in the β1 subunit gene GABRB1
checks.explanation: GABRB1 encodes the GABAA receptor β1 subunit.

paragraphs.text: Janve et al. (2016) reported that the patient carrying a GABRB1 mutation had infantile spasms.

checks.claim: The patient carrying a GABRB1 mutation reported by Janve et al. (2016) had infantile spasms.
checks.evidence_quote: Additionally one IS patient had a mutation in the GABAA receptor β1 subunit gene (GABRB1(F246S)).
checks.explanation: Patient had infantile spasms.

paragraphs.text: Burgess et al. (2019) reported a patient with a GABRB1 mutation whose seizures began in infancy. The patient showed developmental slowing and was classified as having severe to profound impairment.

checks.claim: Burgess et al. (2019) reported a patient with a GABRB1 mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified 2 individuals with pathogenic variants in GABA receptor subunit-encoding genes not previously associated with EIMFS, but reported in association with other developmental and epileptic encephalopathies: one case each for GABRA1 and GABRB1.
checks.explanation: The paper reports a single patient (Patient 63) with a de novo GABRB1 variant, p.I247T.

checks.claim: In the patient with a GABRB1 mutation reported by Burgess et al. (2019), seizures began in infancy.
checks.explanation: Seizure onset was at 4 months.

checks.claim: The patient with a GABRB1 mutation reported by Burgess et al. (2019) showed developmental slowing.
checks.evidence_quote: While all patients showed developmental slowing at the time of refractory migrating focal seizures
checks.explanation: This statement covers all patients in the cohort, so it includes the GABRB1 patient.

checks.claim: The patient with a GABRB1 mutation reported by Burgess et al. (2019) was classified as having severe to profound developmental impairment.
checks.explanation: Table 1 shows 1 GABRB1 patient under 'Profound-severe Impairment'.

paragraphs.text: The GABRB1 mutation reported by Epi4K Consortium et al. (2013) occurred de novo. Janve et al. (2016) stated that the patient was heterozygous for the de novo GABRB1 mutation.

checks.claim: The GABRB1 mutation reported by Epi4K Consortium et al. (2013) occurred de novo.
checks.evidence_quote: we draw attention to the six mutations that all affect subunits of the gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) ionotropic receptor (four in GABRB3, and one each in GABRA1 and GABRB1)
checks.explanation: This sentence comes from the paper's discussion of de novo mutations, so the GABRB1 mutation it lists is a de novo mutation.

checks.claim: The patient with the de novo GABRB1 mutation was heterozygous for the mutation, according to Janve et al. (2016).
checks.evidence_quote: Since the LGS and IS patients were heterozygous for the de novo GABRB3 and GABRB1 mutations
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

paragraphs.text: Epi4K Consortium et al. (2013) carried out trio exome sequencing of patients with infantile spasms or Lennox-Gastaut syndrome and their unaffected parents. In one patient with epileptic encephalopathy, they identified a de novo mutation in the GABRB1 gene.

checks.claim: Epi4K Consortium et al. (2013) carried out trio exome sequencing of patients with infantile spasms or Lennox-Gastaut syndrome and their unaffected parents.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we report a screen for de novo mutations in patients with two classical epileptic encephalopathies: infantile spasms (n = 149) and Lennox-Gastaut syndrome (n = 115). We sequenced the exomes of 264 probands, and their parents, and confirmed 329 de novo mutations.
checks.explanation: The paper describes exome sequencing of trios. On the parents being unaffected, the inclusion criteria say both parents could have no history of seizures, except febrile or metabolic/toxic seizures.

checks.claim: Epi4K Consortium et al. (2013) identified a de novo GABRB1 mutation in one patient with epileptic encephalopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: we draw attention to the six mutations that all affect subunits of the gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) ionotropic receptor (four in GABRB3, and one each in GABRA1 and GABRB1)
checks.explanation: The paper reports one de novo GABRB1 mutation in this cohort of patients with epileptic encephalopathy.

paragraphs.text: Janve et al. (2016) reported that the de novo GABRB1 mutation, a heterozygous phe246-to-ser (F246S) substitution, had been found in a patient with infantile spasms. They expressed this mutation and other de novo GABRB mutations associated with epileptic encephalopathy in heterologous (HEK293T) cells. All of the mutations, including the GABRB1 mutation, impaired GABA-A receptor function. Janve et al. (2016) suggested that GABRB1 is a candidate human epilepsy gene.

checks.claim: The de novo GABRB1 mutation was a heterozygous phe246-to-ser (F246S) substitution, according to Janve et al. (2016).
checks.evidence_quote: Since the LGS and IS patients were heterozygous for the de novo GABRB3 and GABRB1 mutations
checks.explanation: F246S named elsewhere; heterozygosity stated here.

checks.claim: The de novo GABRB1 F246S mutation had been found in a patient with infantile spasms, according to Janve et al. (2016).
checks.evidence_quote: Additionally one IS patient had a mutation in the GABAA receptor β1 subunit gene (GABRB1(F246S)).
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Janve et al. (2016) expressed the GABRB1 F246S mutation and other de novo GABRB mutations associated with epileptic encephalopathy in heterologous HEK293T cells.
checks.evidence_quote: GABAA receptor α1 and γ2L subunits were coexpressed with wild-type and/or mutant β3 or β1 subunits in HEK 293T cells.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: All of the de novo GABRB mutations studied by Janve et al. (2016), including the GABRB1 F246S mutation, impaired GABA-A receptor function.
checks.evidence_quote: All 5 de novo GABRB mutations impaired GABAA receptor function by rearranging conserved structural domains, supporting their role in EEs.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Janve et al. (2016) suggested that GABRB1 is a candidate human epilepsy gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Despite lack of association with epilepsy syndromes, our results suggest GABRB1 as a candidate human epilepsy gene.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

paragraphs.text: Using trio exome sequencing, Epi4K Consortium et al. (2013) identified a de novo GABRB1 mutation in a patient with epileptic encephalopathy. Janve et al. (2016) reported that this was a heterozygous phe246-to-ser (F246S) mutation, found by trio analysis in a patient with infantile spasms. In in vitro studies, Janve et al. (2016) found that the mutation impaired GABA-A receptor function.

checks.claim: Epi4K Consortium et al. (2013) used trio exome sequencing to identify a de novo GABRB1 mutation in a patient with epileptic encephalopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: we draw attention to the six mutations that all affect subunits of the gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) ionotropic receptor (four in GABRB3, and one each in GABRA1 and GABRB1)
checks.explanation: The study used trio exome sequencing (264 trios) and found one de novo GABRB1 mutation in a patient with epileptic encephalopathy.

checks.claim: The de novo GABRB1 mutation was a heterozygous phe246-to-ser (F246S) mutation, according to Janve et al. (2016).
checks.evidence_quote: Since the LGS and IS patients were heterozygous for the de novo GABRB3 and GABRB1 mutations
checks.explanation: Heterozygous de novo F246S mutation stated.

checks.claim: The GABRB1 F246S mutation was found by trio analysis in a patient with infantile spasms, according to Janve et al. (2016).
checks.evidence_quote: By analysis of triads with LGS and IS, three GABRB3 mutations were associated with LGS and one GABRB1 and one GABRB3 mutations were associated with IS
checks.explanation: Trio (triad) analysis in IS stated.

checks.claim: In in vitro studies, Janve et al. (2016) found that the GABRB1 F246S mutation impaired GABA-A receptor function.
checks.evidence_quote: All 5 de novo GABRB mutations impaired GABAA receptor function by rearranging conserved structural domains, supporting their role in EEs.
checks.explanation: Stated directly, based on in vitro HEK293T studies.
